stages.note: Multicloud gets a role in the AWS account. No access key leaves your laptop. Path A creates a new AWS account for Multicloud (recommended); path B connects an account you have. Run every command of this stage in the same terminal and folder. Each change shows its plan first and runs only after your yes.

steps.h: Sign in to Multicloud from the CLI
steps.d: The command prints a link and a code. Open the link in any browser on your computer, sign in with the same account as on multicloud.io, and enter the code. You must be the organization owner. If you belong to more than one organization, add --org <organization-id> to every mctl command.
steps.c:
mctl auth login --no-browser
mctl auth status
steps.g: Use --no-browser on every machine, Windows with WSL included: the browser cannot open from the Linux terminal. It prints a link and a code; open the link in any browser on your computer, sign in, and enter the code.

steps.h: Make a folder for the connection
steps.d: mctl writes the role definition (multicloud.tf) and the OpenTofu state into this folder. Keep the folder after the PoC: you need it to remove the role or close the account later. Use the AWS profile from the previous stage (for path A, the management account).
steps.c:
mkdir multicloud-aws && cd multicloud-aws
export AWS_PROFILE=poc
export AWS_REGION=us-east-1

steps.h: Path A: register a new AWS account
steps.d: Replace <email> with an email address that no AWS account uses (a plus address such as you+multicloud@company.com usually works). Type it twice and compare: a typo creates an account with the wrong email. --allow-quota-requests lets Multicloud file the GPU quota request for you in the next stage; it files each request only after your yes. To file quota yourself, use --no-allow-quota-requests (then you need your own sign-in to the new account).

in.label: Email for the new AWS account

in: Quota requests by Multicloud: yes (recommended) or no
steps.g: This writes multicloud.tf and multicloud.auto.tfvars (the email only) in the folder: keep both. The output has a line like: Next: mctl cloud-account apply 7. The number (here 7) is your cloud-account ID, not an AWS account ID. Write it down. To see it again: mctl cloud-account list

steps.h: Path B: approve the use of an account you have
steps.d: Only for an AWS account that you have. Read this warning first: this account gets a Multicloud IAM role that can start and stop compute and request quota. Existing workloads and their permissions share the account, and its quotas and limits. Removing the connection later means a destroy of the role. Option: a new account (path A), which keeps the PoC apart from your current work. Approve only with an explicit yes. A new account that you made by hand for the PoC holds no other work: it counts as a new account, so say so and continue. If Multicloud reports ACCOUNT_NOT_DEDICATED later, the organization owner runs mctl cloud-account accept-shared-account <cloud-account-id> and types the 12-digit AWS account ID it asks for. Nobody else types it.

steps.h: Path B: register the AWS account you have
steps.d: Replace <account-id> with your 12-digit AWS account ID. Answer two questions: turn on the AWS opt-in regions (yes is the default: Multicloud may use every region and turns on the opt-in regions, for example af-south-1), and let Multicloud file quota requests (recommended: yes; it files each request only after your yes). Write your answers as flags: --no-opt-in-regions for no, --no-allow-quota-requests for no. To limit the regions, add --region <region> once for each region.
in: Quota requests by Multicloud: yes (recommended) or no
steps.g: The output has a line like: Next: mctl cloud-account apply 7. (The line By hand: … after it is for people who apply without mctl; skip it.) The number (here 7) is your cloud-account ID, not your AWS account ID. Write it down. To see it again: mctl cloud-account list. A disconnected (revoked) account: run the same command again; it gets a new number. Reconnect it only with the organization owner's yes.

steps.d: Replace <cloud-account-id> with the number from the register step. The plan changes nothing. Path B: it shows the IAM role and policy that OpenTofu creates in your account. Path A: it shows the new AWS account; the plan of the role can show only after the account exists.

steps.h: Apply: create the account and the role
steps.d: Run it after you read the plan. mctl asks one question: type y. Path A: it creates the AWS account (a few minutes), then the Multicloud role in it; your one yes covers both. Path B: it creates the role. mctl gives OpenTofu a one-time connect token by itself (you never see or paste it), then waits until Multicloud can use the account.
steps.g: AccessDenied on iam:CreateRole: your AWS role cannot create IAM roles. Sign in with AdministratorAccess (aws configure sso --use-device-code) and run the apply again.
